short_answer: Ross Benjamin is a real, long running handicapper. His VegasWinners.com bio says he is 63, lives in Hilton, New York, has handicapped since 2003, wrote and made videos for Sportsbook Review from 2011 to 2017, now writes for the Offshore Gaming Association, and has done radio in Rochester and Akron. One review site says he started out at a Western New York bookmaker. Today he sells mainly through WagerTalk, a Las Vegas pick store, and gives free picks on WagerTalk TV.

His WagerTalk page shows strong streaks, such as 216-147 in college football since the 2023 season and 33-19 in the NFL this season. We checked the math and the win rates match. Each run starts on its own date, though, and WagerTalk both sells and grades the picks. His last 20 graded plays on 19 Nov 2026 were 11-9, about one unit up if each play were one unit.

Forum talk is recent and mixed. On Covers in August and September 2025, members praised his free picks and his YouTube analysis, and some reported winning with them. Others said his paid 3% to 5% plays had a losing week, called a paid pick a coin flip, or asked for a record over a longer period. Older user comments on a review site praised one NBA package but complained about slow replies.

guarantee: WagerTalk sells an optional guarantee on single day picks for a higher price ($23 instead of $15 for one NFL pick). The store's wording is: "The WagerTalk pick guarantee option backs your purchase with 100% in credits." It goes on: "If your daily pick(s) package does not result in an overall profit across all included plays, the paid cash value of a guaranteed pick will be credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase." So a losing guaranteed day returns store credit, not cash, and only what you paid for the pick.

WagerTalk's refund policy treats every sale as final and "as is", with no refund once a product has been bought, delivered or viewed. Its terms cap the company's liability, and the buyer's only remedy, at a refund of the price paid, and describe the information as being for entertainment and amusement only.
We found no guarantee at all on the multi day or season passes, and nothing anywhere covers money lost on the bets themselves.

claims_note: Every streak on the WagerTalk page has its own start date: the 2023 season for college football, 28 Dec 2024 for combined football, 13 Nov 2025 for the NFL, 31 Dec 2025 for college basketball, 13 May 2025 for all sports. A run that starts wherever it looks best is a common way to show a hot stretch. A fair test counts all his plays from a single fixed start date.

His length of service is described differently on each page: "the last 21 years" on WagerTalk, a handicapper since 2003 and about 35 years in the industry on VegasWinners.com, and 13 years as a handicapper on an older Boyd's Bets page.
record: What is independently logged: we found no such record for Benjamin. Rival affiliate pages repeat the same kind of claims (Boyd's Bets says he went 126-103 in the NHL from November 2014, which is 55.0%, and Ride The Hot Hand says 56% in football since 2010 and in hockey since 2012), but none shows a pick by pick log. Ride The Hot Hand says it is paid by some services it reviews.

What the store itself shows: WagerTalk grades his picks, ranks him, and sells them. On 19 Nov 2026 the Last 20 table ran from 12 to 18 Nov and showed 11 wins and 9 losses at odds between -102 and -120. If each play were one unit risked, that is roughly +1 unit over 20 plays. The table does not show his stake sizes, which run from 3% to 5% plays according to forum posts.
His old VegasWinners.com profile still leads with plays for an NFC Championship game between the 49ers and Rams, so it has not been updated in years.

our_data.text: In this edition no Ross Benjamin pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how he performs.

customers_intro: Most of what we found is Covers forum threads from August and September 2025, where members shared and argued about his free and paid picks. We also read user comments on a review site, a 2006 Sportsbook Review thread about his parlay system, and 2026 TheRX threads.

customers.text: We read five Covers threads from August and September 2025 with about 90 posts in all, plus user comments on Handicapping Reviews (up to 2016), one Sportsbook Review thread from 2006 and TheRX threads from 2026. The pattern: his free picks and his WagerTalk TV videos get steady praise, and several members said they made money following the free plays. His paid plays drew more doubt: members reported a run of paid 4% and 5% losses in mid September 2025, one called a paid pick a coin flip, and one asked for a record over a meaningful period. In August 2025 two members noticed his YouTube and X accounts had gone quiet. On the review site, one buyer liked an NBA package enough to buy an NFL package, while another said staff replies were inconsistent. We found no complaint about billing or refunds. Reddit's archive held only two 2020 posts advertising his picks.

A Covers member said they followed Ross Benjamin's free baseball picks on WagerTalk TV and had made over $3,000 in two months with them, and that they planned to buy the paid college football package, splitting the cost with friends. We did not verify the figure.

In the same thread two members asked what had happened to him, since his YouTube channel and X account had no recent posts. A third argued that paying for picks is a mistake and bettors should do their own work, while the first poster defended the college package as good value.

When a member shared what they said were Benjamin's free and paid baseball plays, others pushed back hard on a paid Yankees play, said you get what you pay for, and called the picks a coin flip. Another member in the same thread later praised him.

A Covers member listed four paid 4% and 5% plays from 14 to 16 Sep 2025 that they said had all lost, while saying the free picks had still been profitable for them. Earlier in the thread another member called Benjamin sharp with in depth analysis even on free picks, and another reminded readers that no handicapper wins every time.

A member posted what they said were Benjamin's last 20 plays, 13-7 across the NFL, college football and baseball, and others called him a valuable asset and said they went 2-0 on his free plays. One reply asked whether he had a record over a meaningful period of time. We did not verify these results.

A member in Covers' college football forum called him one of the best college football handicappers, said he was 13-6 for the season, and said his free baseball picks had made that member money. Another member questioned one of the day's picks.

A user comment on Handicapping Reviews said the commenter had a good experience with an NBA package, citing a strong record and upset picks, and then bought a longer NFL package. Another said the picks were pricey but worth it for bettors with a real bankroll.

Other user comments on the same page said staff were inconsistent in answering questions, and that plays released early in the day sometimes came with lines the commenter could no longer get. The site's own reviewer said it was not comfortable with the quality of the picks.

A Sportsbook Review thread discussed a college football parlay system credited to Benjamin, pairing favourite and over against underdog and under when the spread is a large share of the total. Members found the logic interesting but doubted his cutoff and said most books refuse such parlays. One member reported a winning second week with it, another lost both test bets.
On TheRX, members still post his plays in the daily service play threads, and the forum rules list Ross Benjamin among services whose write ups may not be posted.

Our Reddit archive search in r/sportsbetting returned only two posts from August 2020 advertising his picks for $35 and $10; searches in r/sportsbook were rate limited and returned nothing. We found no review or rating for him on VegasWinners.com or WagerTalk itself.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks, grades them, ranks him (#2 in the NFL this season by its own count) and publishes the streak lines, so the store is also the scorekeeper.

WagerTalk posts his free picks on X and YouTube to market the paid packages.
strengths: A long, public career under his real name: Sportsbook Review writer and video analyst 2011 to 2017, OSGA analyst, radio in Rochester and Akron, and a 2008 book mention.
Free picks with full video analysis, which several Covers members said they profited from in 2025.
WagerTalk shows his losses too: the Last 20 table included 9 losing plays.
Cheap ways to try him: $15 single picks and $49 store specials before any season pass.
Every streak win rate we recomputed matched the wins and losses shown.
concerns: Every streak starts on a different date; no full pick history from one fixed date is shown.
The guarantee is a paid extra, repays only store credit and applies to single days, never passes or seasons. All sales are otherwise final.
WagerTalk sells, grades and ranks his picks, so no outside party checks the numbers.
Forum members reported a losing run on his paid 4% and 5% plays in September 2025, and a member said paid picks were a coin flip.
The last 20 graded plays were 11-9, about one unit up: fine, but far from the hot streak banners.
Service length differs by page (21 years, since 2003, 35 years, 13 years), and an old VegasWinners.com profile is years out of date.
checklist: Try a free pick or a $15 single before any pass, and log each play with the line you could actually get.
Ask WagerTalk for every Ross Benjamin play from a fixed date, with stake size, odds and release time.
Keep in mind that a guarantee claim returns store credit, never cash, and only for single day picks.
Count units, not wins: a 55% day table can still be close to break even at -110.
Check the price on the profile and on the specials page; the same access can cost $49 or much more.
Do not chase reposted plays on X or forums; you cannot confirm they are his or that the line is still there.
faq: He is a real, long running handicapper with a public career as a writer and radio guest, and he sells through an established store, WagerTalk. Whether his paid picks beat the market over time is not shown; his records are streaks graded by the store that sells them.
How much does Ross Benjamin cost?

On 19 Nov 2026 WagerTalk listed single picks from $15 ($23 guaranteed), 1 day $39, 3 days $69, 7 days $99, 30 days $299, 90 days $749 and 1 year $1,999, with season passes from $259 to $719 and store specials at $49.
Does Ross Benjamin have a verified record?

No outside log. WagerTalk shows runs such as 216-147 in college football since 2023 and 33-19 in the NFL this season, and his last 20 graded plays were 11-9. We checked the percentages, not the picks.
Does Ross Benjamin offer a refund?
No cash refund. WagerTalk offers a paid guarantee on single day picks; if the day loses, the price comes back as store credit. Passes and seasons are sold as final.
Where does Ross Benjamin sell his picks?
Mainly on WagerTalk.com, which also posts his free picks on WagerTalk TV, X and YouTube. An older profile on VegasWinners.com has not been updated in years.

Bettors on Covers liked his free picks and analysis, but opinions on the paid plays were split. Start with free picks or a single, track the results yourself, and compare against the 52.4% needed at -110.
